name: Socotra White-eye
rangeDescription: Northern somalia and socotra
description: A small, sharp-billed warbler-like bird. Note the yellow throat, pale-gray underparts, and narrow white spectacles around the eyes.

name: Bronzy Jacamar
rangeDescription: Central amazonia, from eastern colombia and southern venezuela eastward to the guianas, southward to southeastern peru (madre de dios), northern bolivia, and south-central amazonian brazil (south to mato grosso)
description: Small, active, and locally distributed. Key field mark is overall bronzy color, which is evident in good light but hard to see otherwise.

name: Inti Tanager
rangeDescription: Incompletely known; breeds in northern bolivia (machariapo valley in la paz); migratory, probably wintering in lower montane forest in southeastern peru, where currently known from a few sightings in cusco (kosñipata valley)
description: A remarkable new species of tanager described to science in 2021. It breeds in and around the Machariapo Valley in western Bolivia from roughly November to March, then disperses northward along the east slope of Andes into southern Peru.

name: White-bellied Heron
rangeDescription: Himalayan foothills (nepal to northeastern india and myanmar)
description: Large, imperious stone-gray heron, very locally distributed and extremely rare. Note dark gray wings, pale throat patch, and white belly.

name: Pale-headed Munia
rangeDescription: Scrub, marshes and ricefields of lowlands of mainland sulawesi and the lesser sundas from lombok eastward through babar
description: A small finch with a striking white head and dark body. Rich chestnut brown above, with reddish tail and pale peach-washed underside.

name: Obscure Berrypecker
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in central and eastern new guinea
description: A small, rare and little-known bird of foothill forest. Medium gray head and back, pale gray throat and chest, and olive flight feathers.

name: Palau Cicadabird
rangeDescription: Palau (western caroline islands)
description: Small cuckooshrike with a restricted range, found only on the Palau Archipelago. Males are mainly gray with a black patch on the face, black tail, and black on the wings.

name: White-headed Vulture
rangeDescription: Thornscrub and desert of sub-saharan africa
description: A medium-sized, mostly dark vulture with an angular, naked, pale pink head and bulky coral-colored beak. In flight, the adult’s white “armpits” extend out as a stripe along the middle of the underwing; the larger females differ from males by having all-white innermost flight feathers.

name: Rufous-winged Sunbird
rangeDescription: Eastern tanzania (eastern escarpment of udzungwa mountains)
description: A small sunbird that is rare within its tiny central Tanzanian range. Both sexes have an unusual bright rufous panel in the wing.

name: Yellow-throated Vireo
rangeDescription: Eastern canada to gulf states; winters to venezuela and west indies
description: Stocky, brightly-colored vireo with yellow throat and spectacles. Olive upperparts and gray wings with two bold white wingbars.

name: Chestnut-backed Thornbird
rangeDescription: Northern peru (upper marañón valley)
description: Handsome bird with a highly restricted range in the Marañon Valley of northern Peru. Back and tail are chestnut with a paler throat, head, and belly; breast is streaked with white.

name: Sinai Rosefinch
rangeDescription: Sinai peninsula
description: A small and long-tailed, small-billed finch. Virtually unstreaked.

name: Black-necked Swan
rangeDescription: Southern brazil to tierra del fuego and falkland islands
description: Basically unmistakable and is just what the name says: a swan with a black neck. Fairly common but sometimes local on lakes, slow-moving rivers, wetlands with open water, estuaries, and inshore coastal waters.

name: Eastern Paradise-Whydah
rangeDescription: Southeastern sudan, ethiopia, and somalia southward to northeastern south africa, also westward across southern africa to angola and northern namibia
description: The breeding male is buff, chestnut, and black with a 21-centimeter tail that is laterally flattened with both short bulging feathers and long, tapering dagger-like feathers. The female and non-breeding male have a strongly contrasting black-and-white head, including a characteristic dark bill and a double “C” pattern under the ear.

name: Dusky Grasswren
rangeDescription: Rocky spinifex hills of central australia
description: Small rusty-brown bird with finely streaked plumage and long cocked tail, found in rocky areas and gorges around spinifex clumps of central Australia, including Alice Springs and Tennant Creek. Upperparts rusty brown, underparts slightly paler brown, the adult female showing a small rusty flank patch.

name: Pinto's Spinetail
rangeDescription: Northeastern brazil (northeastern maranhão, eastern pernambuco, and adjacent alagoas)
description: Spinetail with a largely dark body contrasting with a rich rusty crown, wings, and tail. Note the streaked whitish throat.

name: Ivory-backed Woodswallow
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including lembeh (off northeast), and banggai and sula islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A chunky slate-gray and white bird with a heavy, pale blue bill. A gregarious bird of forest and forest edge in the lowlands and mountains.

name: Striped Crake
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa
description: Small brown crake with conspicuous striping on the back. The underparts are brown in the male and gray in the female.

name: Southern Royal Albatross
rangeDescription: Campbell and auckland islands; ranges circumpolar southern oceans
description: Huge albatross of the Southern Ocean; breeds mainly on Campbell and Auckland Islands in New Zealand, but ranges widely. Easily separated at a distance from smaller albatrosses by white back.

name: White-bellied Go-away-bird
rangeDescription: Acacia savanna of somalia and ethiopia to northeastern tanzania
description: An unusual gray turaco with a long tail and a towering crest. White marks on the sides of the tail are conspicuous in floppy flight.
